title: Bits: Missing Number
oneLiner: n distinct numbers from 0..n, one missing: XOR every index and every value together and the only thing that doesn't cancel is the missing number.
keyTakeaway: XOR together 0, 1, ..., n and every element of the array. Each present number appears twice (once as a possible value, once in the array) and cancels; the missing one appears once and survives. O(n) time, O(1) space, and unlike the sum formula n(n + 1) / 2 it can never overflow.
explanation:
nums holds n distinct numbers taken from the range 0 to n (that's n + 1 possible values), so exactly one value is missing. Return it. For [3, 0, 1], n = 3 and the values 0..3 are 0, 1, 2, 3; 2 is missing.

Three approaches, all fine in an interview, in increasing order of cleverness. A hash set of the values, then check 0..n: O(n) space. Sorting, then look for the first index where nums[i] != i: O(n log n). Or arithmetic: the sum of 0..n is n(n + 1) / 2 (the Gauss pairing trick), and subtracting the array's sum leaves the missing value. That's O(n) and O(1), but in C# n(n + 1) overflows an int once n passes about 46,000 unless you use long. Python has no such limit.

The XOR version has the same O(n) and O(1) and no overflow at all. XOR (^) gives 0 when you combine a number with itself and leaves a number unchanged when you combine it with 0, and the order of XORs doesn't matter. Start with acc = n, then for each index i do acc ^= i ^ nums[i]. Over the loop, acc collects every index 0..n - 1, plus n from the start, which is every value in the range once, and every array element once. Each present value therefore appears twice and cancels, and only the missing one is left.

It's the Single Number trick in disguise: imagine appending 0..n to the array, and now every value appears twice except the missing one.

The visualization runs [3, 0, 1]. The tracker is acc.

visualizationSteps.message: nums = [3, 0, 1], n = 3, so the values should be 0, 1, 2, 3. No index equals 3, so seed acc = 3.
Altogether acc = 3 ^ 0 ^ 3 ^ 1 ^ 0 ^ 2 ^ 1: the 0s, 1s and 3s cancel in pairs, leaving 2, the missing number.

recognitionSignals: "Numbers 0..n (or 1..n) with one missing", or one duplicated, and O(1) extra space.
The array's values are a known range, so the indexes themselves can be paired against the values.
A sum-based answer exists but you're asked about overflow, or values are large.
gotchas: The range is 0..n inclusive, which is one more value than the array holds: seed acc with n (or loop i to n).
If you use the sum formula in C#, compute it in long: n * (n + 1) as int overflows for n above 46,340.
Sorting and scanning works but changes the input and is O(n log n); say so if you choose it.
confusableWith: Single Number (this track): same XOR cancellation, but there the pairs are already in the array.
Cyclic sort / index marking ("first missing positive") puts each value at its own index; it handles harder variants but rewrites the array.

complexity.note: One pass XOR-ing each index and value into one accumulator; no set, no sort, no overflow.
